## The curriculum is now organized as courses

The lesson URLs have not changed, but the former 14-chapter path is now divided
into five focused courses with explicit prerequisites.

[Open the course catalog](../courses/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Compare the pathways](../pathways/index.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

::: {.course-grid}
::: {.course-card}
### [Python Foundations](../courses/python-foundations/index.qmd)

Getting Started, Core Python, Data Structures, Functions, and Debugging.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### [Intermediate Python](../courses/intermediate-python/index.qmd)

Files and Data, Projects and Environments, Code Quality, and Object-Oriented
Python.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### [Advanced Python Engineering](../courses/advanced-python/index.qmd)

Advanced patterns now, with deeper engineering modules planned.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### [Scientific Computing](../courses/scientific-python/index.qmd)

NumPy, simulation, Matplotlib, SymPy, and SciPy.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### [Data Science and Machine Learning](../courses/data-science-ml/index.qmd)

Data workflows, visualization, model training, AI libraries, and responsible AI.
:::
:::

<!-- fcpython-chapter-lab: start -->
## A practical study routine

For each lesson, predict the result, run the smallest example, explain what
happened, change one thing, and use errors as evidence. Study one lesson deeply
instead of skimming an entire course.
<!-- fcpython-chapter-lab: end -->
